role: ONE proposed host process-boundary experiment, not executed and not an additional project plan
decision: Limited per-process mechanisms are source-supported; complete decoder-resource/secrecy/total-wall/subtree containment is not established.
host_scope: Existing R00 CPython3.12.15 on identified Linux host; no install or R00 changes. Deterministic helper modes, no selected decoder/backend/production port.
fixture_role: Exact13949 response-get-public-key rawRGB/public envelope references in source-bindings.json. Helper positive returns predetermined bytes only; actual_QR_decode=false and crypto/key operations=false.
parameter_rules: All finite, typed and frozen before execution; checked arithmetic and explicit inherited-limit handling. No silent increase after failure.

Worker AS is virtual address space; no RSS/cumulative-allocation/parent/kernel-memory claim. Existing bootstrap usage is not reclaimed by setrlimit. A strict startup ceiling/accounting is unqualified, and unsupported admission must be refused.
CPU units are seconds; wall is monotonic result eligibility and cleanup initiation, not a hard return-time guarantee. No mapping from manual-port logical parse_work/retained bytes.
Caller limits must be applied/read back before hostile input is sent/read or decoder/image work begins; no preexec_fn or privileged fallback.
setup_to_record: Exact trusted executable/helper source/environment/argv hashes; kernel/libc/Python ABI and UID/GID/privilege context; no secrets supplied.
Spawn begin/return, PID/session/group, requested/read-back rlimits, policy gate and first hostile-byte transfer timestamps.
Input/output/stderr retained and total-observed byte counters, overflow reason, cancellation/deadline, signal attempts, actual direct-child wait status and owned I/O/callback settlement.
Exclusive wait ownership; missing/stolen status is an error. Any fixture descendants and final cleanup state are explicit.

cases.trigger: One fixed public raw image buffer and predetermined public envelope returned by a keyless deterministic helper after policy gate.
cases.expect: Exact output bytes, all byte counters within declared caps, policy readback recorded, actual child status successful and owned I/O/callbacks settled before reuse. This is IPC/resource feasibility, NOT QR decoding or signing.

cases.trigger: Hold one valid raw buffer/metadata tuple fixed; lower only its declared width, height or pixel cap below the actual value, in separate rows. A separate stride/length relation row keeps dimensional caps nonbinding.
cases.expect: Refuse before spawn/conversion/copy; hostile bytes transferred0. Keep these rows separate from raw-cap refusal.

cases.trigger: Hold one valid raw buffer and dimensions/stride fixed, with byte length N. Vary only the declared raw cap N-1/N/N+1; dimension checks remain valid.
cases.expect: Cap N-1 refuses before spawn/transfer; caps N/N+1 reach the intended next boundary. No dimension/length mismatch may mask the raw-cap row.

cases.trigger: Unsupported/permission-failed AS or CPU setting, readback mismatch, or impossible startup policy.
cases.expect: No hostile input or eligible output. Do not mistake successful lowering below existing usage for a reclaimed/fully bounded bootstrap; record the accounting gap or refusal. No privilege elevation or silent fallback.

cases.trigger: After policy is established, helper attempts a new mapping/allocation beyond finite AS while stdout/stderr/CPU/wall remain nonbinding.
cases.expect: Record actual allocation failure/process termination and readback; no eligible output. Bootstrap failure instead means this row was not exercised. No RSS/cumulative-allocation conclusion.

cases.trigger: Helper spins after policy gate, with pipe/AS limits nonbinding and a wall allowance that does not win first.
cases.expect: Record limit-related termination/signal and actual status; a parent wall kill is not CPU-limit proof. CPU-seconds observation does not prove logical parse_work or realtime latency.

cases.trigger: Helper waits without consuming substantial CPU beyond the declared monotonic wall eligibility deadline.
cases.expect: Result invalidated, terminate/kill as needed, actual wait and I/O settlement precede reuse. Delayed completion stays ineligible; no promise of bounded spawn/kill/reap latency.

cases.trigger: Helper emits output beyond its cap while stderr is quiet and other limits do not fire first.
cases.expect: Retained output never exceeds its own cap; temporary reads stay within the separately declared fixed chunk. Refuse on overflow before append, keep explicit bounded/truncated diagnostics, stop/collect worker; never capture entire flood.

cases.trigger: Helper emits diagnostics beyond their cap while stdout is bounded and other limits do not fire first.
cases.expect: Retained diagnostics never exceed their own cap; temporary reads stay within the separately declared fixed chunk. Independent stderr refusal/cleanup; stdout overflow or earlier CPU/wall failure gives no stderr-cap credit.

cases.trigger: Helper stops reading its gated input.
cases.expect: Supervision remains responsive; blocked write cannot release ownership or grow queued input without bound. Cleanup/actual status precede reuse.

cases.trigger: Cancel separately during pending startup, input/scan work, and after bytes arrive before cleanup settles.
cases.expect: No late eligible output. Reservation remains until real cessation/settlement; unknown cleanup rejects/quarantines. Delayed bootstrap is not evidence that uninterruptible Popen creation was tested.

cases.trigger: Controlled helper leaves a known descendant holding a pipe, or actual child status/cleanup cannot be obtained.
cases.expect: Direct child exit/EOF/signal success alone cannot mark reuse. Known group members are signalled/collected where owned; unresolved/escaped ownership or status remains quarantined. Test fixture cleanup is explicit; do not generalize to a compromised process subtree.

unproven_after_this_experiment: Uninterruptible process creation or a universal hard wall/kill/reap latency ceiling
RSS/cumulative allocation/total job or kernel resources, logical decoder work
Compromised/privileged worker or arbitrary escaped descendants, access to parent memory/files/keys
Actual decoder, camera/ARM/Pi, actual TypeScript driver integration, trusted UI/physical approval
acceptance: Every row must reach its intended boundary; earlier/masking failures are NOT_EXERCISED, not PASS. A bounded success plus isolated negative observations qualifies only this host process-boundary experiment. Preserve actual failures/configs and refuse reuse where quiescence is unknown.

parameter_units.dimension_pixel_stride_byte_caps: Finite positive integers; checked products and exact available raw length; no conversion/worker transfer before validation.
parameter_units.worker_AS_bytes: Finite positive integer; Linux virtual-address-space semantics/page granularity, bootstrap accounting not automatically covered.
parameter_units.CPU_limits: Finite positive integer seconds, soft<=hard; zero/unknown/infinite values are not this experiment policy.
parameter_units.wall_and_cleanup: Finite positive monotonic durations; eligibility/observation windows only, no hard realtime or guaranteed spawn/reap latency.
parameter_units.IO: Separate output/diagnostic retained caps and a finite positive read/write chunk. Temporary chunk storage is separately accounted; never appended beyond each retained cap.
